answer: To resist sybil attacks, the network runs a jury lottery each epoch: identities are randomly shuffled into small audit juries that must verify one another's ledger work before any payout clears from the shared vault. An attacker's fresh, hollow personas get scattered across juries instead of clustered, so they cannot vouch for themselves; they would need to outnumber every jury, which costs real attestation labor per seat. Like a reef, strength comes from many independent polyps — correlated, centrally-controlled agents can't blend in.
